spec_says.text: Multiple force_flush() calls coalesce into single flush operation

code_does.text: Ticket-based: calls registered before a pass reads `requested` share that pass; calls registered mid-pass wait for the next; with nothing dirty there is no I/O but one worker wake-up

edits.old: | FR-12 | Multiple `force_flush()` calls coalesce into single flush operation | Implemented |
edits.new: | FR-12 | Concurrent `force_flush()` / `FlushManager::trigger_flush()` calls coalesce: each call registers a request (ticket) before waking the worker; a flush pass serves every request registered before it reads the request counter and snapshots the store, so all of them are released by that one pass. A call registered while a pass is already in flight is not released by that pass (its writes may postdate the snapshot); it is served, together with every other call registered meanwhile, by the next pass. No call is ever released by a flush whose snapshot predates the call | Implemented (`src/flush.rs:88-94`, `:152-178`, `:211-213`, `:251-257`) |

edits.old: - Multiple concurrent `force_flush()` calls coalesce into a single flush operation
edits.new: - Concurrent `force_flush()` calls coalesce: all calls registered before a flush pass begins are released by that pass; calls registered while a pass is in flight wait for, and share, the next pass, whose snapshot includes their writes

edits.old: - When no entries are dirty, `force_flush()` returns immediately (no-op)
edits.new: - When no entries are dirty, `force_flush()` performs no disk I/O: the flush worker observes a zero dirty count and releases the caller without flushing (one worker wake-up, no flush)

spec_says.text: FlushManager provides background flush with timer + dirty threshold

code_does.text: Timer deadline recomputed each wait (None disables it); threshold = max(dirty_threshold,1), polled every 10 ms; threshold disarmed after a failed flush until a later pass succeeds

edits.old: | FR-11 | `FlushManager` provides background flush with timer + dirty threshold | Implemented |
edits.new: | FR-11 | `FlushManager` provides background flush with two triggers. (a) Timer: a pass runs once `FlushConfig::interval` (default 5 s) has elapsed since the worker last began waiting; an interval too large to add to the current `Instant` disables the timer. (b) Dirty threshold: a pass runs as soon as `dirty_count() >= max(dirty_threshold, 1)` (default 100), detected within at most 10 ms (`THRESHOLD_POLL_INTERVAL`) because `put`/`delete` do not wake the worker. A failed flush disarms the threshold trigger until a later pass succeeds, so a failing device is retried on the timer or by an explicit `trigger_flush()` rather than in a hot loop. A timer pass with nothing dirty does no I/O | Implemented (`src/flush.rs:14-16`, `:59-75`, `:185-206`, `:234`) |

spec_says.text: Dirty count tracks mutations since last flush; FR-17 lists snapshot_entries/mark_flushed without semantics; plan.md:101 'reset dirty_count'

code_does.text: snapshot_entries records the dirty count it covers; mark_flushed subtracts exactly that count and clears it (no-op without a snapshot); a single recorded slot implies a single-flusher precondition

edits.old: | FR-14 | Dirty count tracks mutations since last flush | Implemented |
edits.new: | FR-14 | Dirty count tracks mutations not yet covered by a successful flush: `put` and `delete` each increment it after releasing the store write lock; a successful flush subtracts only the count recorded with the snapshot it wrote, so mutations made after that snapshot (including during the flush) stay dirty and are persisted by a later flush; a failed flush subtracts nothing; `load_entries` resets it to 0 | Implemented (`src/lib.rs:86-121`, `:188`, `:209`) |

edits.old: | FR-17 | External persistence-wiring API (`initialize_from_client`, `snapshot_entries`, `mark_flushed`, `load_entries`, `dirty_count()`, `flush_seq()` on `ExtendedMetadataStoreComponent`) provides the startup-recovery and flush-on-demand mechanism for persistent-mode deployments; a caller/dispatcher wires a `BlockDeviceClient` and drives these methods (directly or via `FlushManager`) to obtain durability | Implemented |
edits.new: | FR-17 | External persistence-wiring API (`initialize_from_client`, `snapshot_entries`, `mark_flushed`, `load_entries`, `dirty_count()`, `flush_seq()` on `ExtendedMetadataStoreComponent`) provides the startup-recovery and flush-on-demand mechanism for persistent-mode deployments; a caller/dispatcher wires a `BlockDeviceClient` and drives these methods (directly or via `FlushManager`) to obtain durability. `snapshot_entries()` records the dirty count its snapshot covers; `mark_flushed(seq)` sets `flush_seq` to `seq` and subtracts exactly that recorded count, then clears it. Callers MUST therefore call `mark_flushed` only after successfully persisting the entries returned by the immediately preceding `snapshot_entries()`, and only one flusher (one `FlushManager`, or one manual caller) may drive the snapshot/mark pair at a time: an interleaved second `snapshot_entries()` overwrites the recorded count. `mark_flushed` with no preceding snapshot leaves the dirty count unchanged | Implemented (`src/lib.rs:50-53`, `:96-121`) |

spec_says.text: FlushManager performs final flush on Drop (graceful shutdown); FlushManager: Background flush thread with configurable timer/threshold, coalesced flush support

code_does.text: The final pass flushes unconditionally (even when clean) and its result is ignored; public completed_seq() accessor

edits.old: | FR-13 | `FlushManager` performs final flush on Drop (graceful shutdown) | Implemented |
edits.new: | FR-13 | `FlushManager` performs a final flush on Drop (graceful shutdown): Drop sets the shutdown flag, wakes the worker and joins it; the worker runs one last flush pass unconditionally (even with a zero dirty count, which writes a fresh region and advances `flush_seq`) and exits. A failure of this final flush is not reported to the dropping thread | Implemented (`src/flush.rs:215-219`, `:263-277`) |
